name: Civita di Bagnoregio (the pinnacle)
tagline: The dying town itself, car-free and suspended above the badlands
description: The hamlet proper, reached only by the long pedestrian footbridge, holds a handful of permanent residents, a few restaurants, guest rooms, and stone lanes largely unchanged for centuries. Magical at dawn and dusk once day-trippers leave, but with almost no daily-life infrastructure and heavy midday crowds.
bestFor: short stays, photographers, honeymooners, sunrise and sunset chasers
pros: Unmatched views over the calanchi badlands
Car-free, silent evenings once crowds clear
cons: No shops, pharmacy, or real services
Entry ticket and footbridge for every errand

name: Bagnoregio (town centre)
tagline: The practical base, five minutes from the bridge to Civita
description: The larger town most visitors and would-be nomads actually stay in, with Piazza Cavour, the Belvedere viewpoint over Civita, small groceries, cafes, and modest apartment rentals. Everyday Italian small-town life with the postcard view a short walk away.
bestFor: budget-conscious stays, longer visits, anyone needing basic services
pros: Affordable rent versus Civita or Orvieto
Belvedere gives the classic Civita view for free
Real shops and a resident community
cons: Bus service to Orvieto is sparse, especially Sundays

name: Mercatello / the footbridge approach
tagline: The car park and gateway hamlet at the foot of the bridge
description: A small cluster of parking areas, a few shops, and the ticket booths where the footbridge to Civita begins. Functional rather than charming, but the most convenient spot for anyone driving in or needing quick access to both Bagnoregio and Civita without the steepest walking.
bestFor: day-trip logistics, drivers, quick access to the bridge
pros: Closest parking to the Civita footbridge
Good staging point for calanchi viewpoints
cons: Little atmosphere or reason to linger
Very few dining or lodging options directly here

name: Orvieto
tagline: The nearby rail hub with real infrastructure and nomad-friendly cafes
description: A larger hilltop town roughly 25 minutes away by car or bus, on the main Rome-Florence rail line, with a Gothic cathedral, historic cafes, more housing stock, and steady cafe culture. The realistic base for anyone who wants a Tuscia-area lifestyle with better connectivity and services.
bestFor: remote workers wanting real coworking cafes, travelers using trains, longer bases
pros: Direct rail access to Rome and Florence
Far more dining, shops, and services
cons: Not walkable to Civita, still needs a bus or car
More tourist traffic and higher prices than Bagnoregio
